lean.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ)
    (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (R : ℝ) (hR : 0 < R)
    (hu : ∃ v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ,
      InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd v (Metric.closedBall a R) ∧
      Set.EqOn v u (Metric.closedBall a R)),
    let τ : MeasureTheory.Measure (Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1) :=
      (MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))).toSphere
    ∃ v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ,
      InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd v (Metric.closedBall a R) ∧
      Set.EqOn v u (Metric.closedBall a R) ∧
      ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ R →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ζ : Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1 =>
          inner ℝ (gradient v (a + r • ζ.1)) ζ.1) τ ∧
        (∫ ζ : Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1,
          inner ℝ (gradient v (a + r • ζ.1)) ζ.1 ∂τ) = 0
approved_definition_context: EuclideanSpace real (Fin n) has the standard real n-dimensional l2 norm and inner product; n is a natural number. Natural subtraction is truncated.
ContDiffAt real k f x for finite k means actual local continuous real differentiability of order k at x, on a neighborhood of x.

The volume measure is actual Lebesgue volume. Its toSphere law is the unnormalized polar measure on the unit-sphere subtype: for a measurable unit-sphere set S its measure is n times volume of the cone {r*zeta:0<r<1,zeta in S}. In dimension zero this law is zero.
Integrable means actual scalar L1 for the specified measure; IntegrableOn uses its restriction to the stated set. The integral is the real Bochner integral, whose equality alone does not assert L1.

gradient f is the Riesz representative of the actual real Fréchet derivative. HarmonicOnNhd f S means that at every x in S, f is locally C2 and its actual Euclidean Laplacian is zero on a neighborhood of x.

EqOn v u K means pointwise equality at every point of K. It gives no regularity of the total u outside K. An existential function outside a universal radius quantifier is one fixed function for all those radii.
